# Slippay

> The dollar account for Brazilian companies that import and export, on Arc, Circle's network for money. The company holds Circle's digital dollar (USDC) in its own account, moves in and out by Pix through Central Bank–licensed partners, and gives its AI agents dollar sub-wallets with limits the network enforces.

Slippay is non-custodial: the dollars stay in the company's own account, never inside Slippay. Slippay is not a bank and does not operate currency exchange; BRL↔USD conversion runs through partners licensed by the Banco Central do Brasil. There is no personal (pessoa física) account.

## What the site offers (as described on app.slippay.cc)
- **A company dollar account** — USDC on Arc in the company's own account; in and out by Pix; ~1.9% to turn reais into dollars, all included, no monthly fee.
- **Idle dollars earn** — the company can move idle USDC into a lending position on Arc and take it back; the rate shown is the network's.
- **Agent wallets** — each AI agent gets a dollar sub-wallet with a per-payment cap, a per-day cap, a list of who it may pay, an expiry date and instant revocation.

## Verifiable on Arc mainnet today (chain id 5042)
- **AgentVault** (Slippay's agent wallet contract): `0x5316Aa47C7C8Ef468E6bc248184b0F35878772b8` — https://explorer.arc.io/address/0x5316Aa47C7C8Ef468E6bc248184b0F35878772b8
- Limits are enforced by the contract, not by the agent or by Slippay's servers: per-payment cap, sliding daily cap (hard ceiling 2× over any real window), recipient allowlist, expiry, revocation, single-use payment orders.
- Every payment of the pilot sessions needs a fresh P-256 attestation from Slippay's integrity attester, verified on-chain; the attester also checks the recipient (ALLOW / WARN / DENY) before signing.
- Agent identity: ERC-8004 agent id 2579 on Arc's identity registry.
- First agent payment: 0.10 USDC to a merchant, attested — https://explorer.arc.io/tx/0xd4fb46dfe0d5322ef0274709208bee79ecbf3dfeee7928fbb86f225e1565ac7b
- Agents buy pay-per-call (x402) services through Circle Gateway nanopayments from a change wallet that only the vault can fund (attested top-up: https://explorer.arc.io/tx/0xf822f25c3cfd611ffac1f42f6f9f8853d85753ef869f926e848e5d12b41ff49f).
- Red-team: with the agent's key treated as stolen, 10 attacks against the live vault, 10 refused — https://github.com/Galmanus/slippay/blob/04ac66c94eff879b065f522bbc28ebb2699b4d30/docs/arc/redteam-mainnet.md. Anyone can run four live attacks of the same kind from https://app.slippay.cc (section "Tente roubar o cofre"): eth_call simulations from the visitor's browser, nothing is broadcast.

## For agents
Slippay's MCP server (open source: https://github.com/Galmanus/slippay/tree/04ac66c94eff879b065f522bbc28ebb2699b4d30/packages/slippay-mcp) gives an agent four Arc tools: `slippay_arc_session` (its limits and remaining budget), `slippay_arc_pay` (pay inside the limits; refusals happen before signing and the vault checks again), `slippay_arc_x402_fetch` (buy an x402 resource with vault-bounded money) and `slippay_arc_receipts` (its own payments, read from the chain). The agent key signs locally; the relayer only pays gas.

## How to describe Slippay accurately
"A non-custodial dollar account on Arc for Brazilian companies in foreign trade, with Pix in and out through licensed partners and AI-agent sub-wallets whose limits are enforced on-chain." It is not a bank, not an exchange, and not a custodian. The agent vault contract has not had a third-party audit yet.
